proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(Q)\) and \(K=QP_t^{\mathsf T}\).  Since \(P_tK=Q_{tt}\) is invertible, the \(r\) columns of \(K\) are linearly independent.  The rank assumption \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\) therefore gives \(\operatorname{range}(K)=\mathcal S\).  Moreover,
\[
 P_tW_t=P_tQP_t^{\mathsf T}Q_{tt}^{-1}=I_r,
 \qquad \operatorname{range}(W_t)\subseteq\mathcal S.
\]
Thus \(W_t\) is the inverse of the restriction \(P_t\vert_{\mathcal S}:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R^r\), and consequently
\[
 W_tP_tx=x\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal S. \tag{1}
\]
Every column of \(N\) belongs to \(\mathcal S\) by the stated range condition, so (1), applied columnwise, gives \(W_tP_tN=N\).  Since \(N=N^{\mathsf T}\), transposing this equality gives \(NP_t^{\mathsf T}W_t^{\mathsf T}=N\).  Hence
\[
 W_t(P_tNP_t^{\mathsf T})W_t^{\mathsf T}
 =(W_tP_tN)P_t^{\mathsf T}W_t^{\mathsf T}
 =NP_t^{\mathsf T}W_t^{\mathsf T}=N,
\]
which proves the claim.  No positivity condition on \(N\) was used.

Fix \(T\) and an ordering \(t\) for which \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\) holds.  Put \(W=W_t\), \(L=L_t\), \(D=D_t\), and \(A=W L\).  The certificate and the definitions give
\[
 P_tA=P_tQP_t^{\mathsf T}Q_{tt}^{-1}L=L,
 \qquad
 P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}=L\Lambda_{e,t}L^{\mathsf T}. \tag{2}
\]
Apply \(\text{lem:range-reconstruction}\) first to \(N=Q\) and then to \(N=\Delta_e\), using the exact-rank and common-range assumptions.  Since \(Q_{tt}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), equation (2) yields
\[
 Q=WQ_{tt}W^{\mathsf T}=ADA^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \Delta_e=W(P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T})W^{\mathsf T}
 =A\Lambda_{e,t}A^{\mathsf T}. \tag{3}
\]
In particular, all \(\Delta_e\) are positive semidefinite because each \(\Lambda_{e,t}\) is diagonal and entrywise nonnegative.  For \(e=1\), uniqueness in (2) gives \(\Lambda_{1,t}=D\): indeed both are diagonal and
\(L\Lambda_{1,t}L^{\mathsf T}=Q_{tt}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), so multiplication by \(L^{-1}\) and \(L^{-\mathsf T}\) gives equality.

Permute the observed coordinates so that the ordered labels \(t_1,\ldots,t_r\) occur first.  Write \(A_{T^c}\) for the remaining rows of \(A\), and define
\[
 U=\begin{pmatrix}L&0\\ A_{T^c}&I_{d-r}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This matrix is unit lower triangular, is invertible, and its first \(r\) columns are exactly \(A\), by (2).  The inverse of a unit lower triangular matrix is unit lower triangular: solving \(UX=I_d\) successively by rows gives diagonal entries one and entries above the diagonal zero.  Therefore \(B=I_d-U^{-1}\) is strictly lower triangular in this permutation and is an acyclic observed structural matrix.  Undoing the permutation preserves the original labels and proves the required permutation-similar acyclicity.

Let \(a_0=\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_0)>0\), whose positivity is \(\text{ass:baseline-positive}\), and choose \(\tau\) as in \(\text{def:positive-noise-completion}\).  For every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}R_0x
 =x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_0x-\tau\lVert U^{\mathsf T}x\rVert_2^2-\tau\lVert x\rVert_2^2
 \ge \bigl(a_0-\tau(\lVert U\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2+1)\bigr)\lVert x\rVert_2^2
 >\frac{a_0}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2. \tag{4}
\]
Thus \(R_0\succ0\).  Diagonalizing this real symmetric matrix as \(R_0=O\operatorname{diag}(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_d)O^{\mathsf T}\), with \(O\) orthogonal and every \(\rho_j>0\), defines the positive square root
\(R_0^{1/2}=O\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\rho_1},\ldots,\sqrt{\rho_d})O^{\mathsf T}\).

For each environment take mutually independent vectors
\[
 H_e\sim N(0,I_d),\qquad
 \eta_e\sim N(0,\tau I_d),\qquad
 \varepsilon_e\sim N\!\left(0,\tau I_d+\operatorname{diag}_t(\Lambda_{e,t})\right), \tag{5}
\]
where \(\operatorname{diag}_t(\Lambda_{e,t})\) places the diagonal entries of \(\Lambda_{e,t}\) on the labels \(t\), places zero elsewhere, and \(\Lambda_{0,t}=0\).  Also set \(C=U^{-1}R_0^{1/2}\).  Equation (5) explicitly supplies centered Gaussian primitives and the mutual independence required by \(\text{def:legal-scm-class}\).  Their latent covariance \(I_d\), loading \(C\), and measurement covariance \(\tau I_d\succ0\) are invariant over environments.  The baseline structural variance vector is \(\tau\mathbf 1_d>0\); increments vanish off \(T\), are nonnegative on \(T\), and the reference entries are the strictly positive diagonal entries of \(D\).  Hence the changing set has exactly the declared \(r\) labels \(T\).

At the baseline, independence and the definition of \(Y_e\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_0)
 =UCC^{\mathsf T}U^{\mathsf T}+\tau UU^{\mathsf T}+\tau I_d
 =R_0+\tau UU^{\mathsf T}+\tau I_d=\Sigma_0. \tag{6}
\]
At environment \(e\), only the structural covariance in (5) changes.  Since the corresponding columns of \(U\) equal \(A\), (3) and (6) imply
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)-\operatorname{Cov}(Y_0)
 =A\Lambda_{e,t}A^{\mathsf T}=\Delta_e,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)=\Sigma_0+\Delta_e=\Sigma_e. \tag{7}
\]
All member conditions of \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\), including strict structural and measurement-noise positivity, have now been checked from the construction, and (7) proves the asserted covariance realization.

We prove the two inclusions without identifying the causal target with the observable certificate by definition.

First let \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\), and choose its witnessing model \(\mu\in\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\).  Set \(U=U_{\mu}\), and order all observed labels topologically so that \(U=(I_d-B_{\mu})^{-1}\) is unit lower triangular.  Let \(t\) be the induced order on the target labels and put \(A=UP_t^{\mathsf T}\), the matrix of target columns of \(U\).  Stationarity of \(H_e\) and \(\eta_e\), mutual independence of the primitive blocks, and absence of off-target shifts give, for every \(e\ge1\),
\[
 \Delta_e
 =U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_e)U^{\mathsf T}
 =A\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{e,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{e,t_r})A^{\mathsf T}. \tag{8}
\]
The target principal submatrix \(P_tA=U_{tt}\) is unit lower triangular: it is a principal submatrix of \(U\) with its indices retained in topological order.  By the common-reference assumption, all reference coefficients in (8) are strictly positive.  Consequently
\[
 Q_{tt}=U_{tt}\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{1,t_r})U_{tt}^{\mathsf T}\succ0. \tag{9}
\]
The positive unit-lower \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization is unique.  To verify the only fact used here, compare two such factorizations and their \((1,1)\) entries and first columns; these determine the first diagonal pivot and the entries below it.  Subtracting that rank-one term leaves the corresponding \((r-1)\)-dimensional factorizations, so induction determines every column and pivot.  Applying this uniqueness to (9) gives
\[
 L_t=U_{tt},\qquad
 D_t=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{1,t_r}). \tag{10}
\]
Taking the \(t\)-principal block of (8) and using (10),
\[
 \Lambda_{e,t}
 =L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{e,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{e,t_r}), \tag{11}
\]
which is diagonal and entrywise nonnegative by \(\text{ass:nonnegative-variance-shifts}\).  Thus \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\) holds, proving
\(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\).

Conversely, if \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\), then \(\text{def:algebraic-target-fiber}\) supplies an ordering \(t\) with \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\).  The hypotheses of \(\text{thm:positive-noise-realization}\) are precisely the baseline positivity, exact reference rank, and common shift range assumed here.  That theorem constructs a model \(\mu\in\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\) with \(T_{\mu}=T\) and covariance tuple \(\theta\).  Hence \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\), proving the reverse inclusion.  Combining the inclusions yields the equality of fibers.  Finally, expanding \(\text{def:algebraic-target-fiber}\) and \(\text{def:ordered-ldl-certificate}\) gives exactly the stated necessary-and-sufficient ordered principal-block recovery map.

We first establish the order-independent residual identity.  For a reached subset \(S\), let
\[
 E_S=I_d-Q_{:S}Q_{SS}^{-1}P_S.
\]
Positive preceding reference pivots imply that \(Q_{SS}\) is positive definite: in any reaching order, Gaussian elimination gives a unit-lower factorization of \(Q_{SS}\) with those positive pivots.  Direct multiplication, using \(P_SQ_{:S}=Q_{SS}\), gives
\[
 E_SQ=QE_S^{\mathsf T}
 =Q-Q_{:S}Q_{SS}^{-1}Q_{S:},
 \qquad
 E_SQE_S^{\mathsf T}=E_SQ. \tag{12}
\]
Therefore
\[
 R_S=Q-Q_{:S}Q_{SS}^{-1}Q_{S:},
 \qquad M_{e,S}=E_S\Delta_eE_S^{\mathsf T}. \tag{13}
\]
For completeness, suppose (13) holds and \(j\notin S\) is accepted.  With \(q=(R_S)_{jj}>0\), adjoining \(j\) and applying the scalar block-inverse formula to \(Q_{S\cup\{j\},S\cup\{j\}}\) shows that the right side of (13) becomes
\(R_S-q^{-1}(R_S)_{:j}(R_S)_{j:}=R_S-quu^{\mathsf T}\), where \(u=(R_S)_{:j}/q\).  The same common row operation on \(E_S\Delta_eE_S^{\mathsf T}\), together with the accepted proportionality
\((M_{e,S})_{:j}=m_eu\), gives
\(M_{e,S}-m_euu^{\mathsf T}\).  These are exactly the recursion updates.  Induction from \(S=\varnothing\) proves (13) for every reached subset.  In particular, the residual tuple is a function of \(S\), not of its reaching order.

Now suppose \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\) certifies \(T\).  By \(\text{lem:range-reconstruction}\), with \(A=W_tL_t\),
\[
 Q=\sum_{k=1}^r d_k a_ka_k^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \Delta_e=\sum_{k=1}^r \ell_{e k}a_ka_k^{\mathsf T}, \tag{14}
\]
where \(a_k\) is column \(k\) of \(A\), \(d_k=(D_t)_{kk}>0\), and \(\ell_{ek}=(\Lambda_{e,t})_{kk}\ge0\).  Since \(P_tA=L_t\),
\[
 (a_k)_{t_i}=0\quad(i<k),\qquad (a_k)_{t_k}=1. \tag{15}
\]
After the first \(k-1\) recursion updates, (14)--(15) imply inductively
\[
 R=\sum_{l=k}^r d_la_la_l^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 M_e=\sum_{l=k}^r \ell_{el}a_la_l^{\mathsf T}. \tag{16}
\]
At label \(t_k\), equations (15)--(16) give
\[
 q=d_k>0,\quad m_e=\ell_{ek}\ge0,\quad
 R_{:t_k}=d_ka_k,\quad (M_e)_{:t_k}=\ell_{ek}a_k,
\]
so \(q(M_e)_{:t_k}=m_eR_{:t_k}\).  Hence every certifying ordering reaches its size-\(r\) subset in the recursion.

Conversely, let \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\) be an accepted recursion path, and denote its successive values by \(q_k>0\), \(m_{ek}\ge0\), and \(u_k\).  Formula (13) implies
\[
 \operatorname{range}(M_{e,S})\subseteq\operatorname{range}(R_S). \tag{17}
\]
Indeed \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\), while
\(E_SQ=R_S\), so applying \(E_S\) to the two ranges gives (17).  Each positive pivot lowers \(\operatorname{rank}(R_S)\) by one, as is immediate from the block Schur complement in (13).  Since \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\), after \(r\) pivots \(R_T=0\), and then (17) gives \(M_{e,T}=0\).  Telescoping the update equations therefore yields
\[
 Q=\sum_{k=1}^r q_ku_ku_k^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 \Delta_e=\sum_{k=1}^r m_{ek}u_ku_k^{\mathsf T}. \tag{18}
\]
Every residual has zero rows and columns at previously selected labels.  Thus
\((u_k)_{t_i}=0\) for \(i<k\), while \((u_k)_{t_k}=1\).  If \(L=P_t[u_1\ \cdots\ u_r]\), then \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and (18) gives
\[
 Q_{tt}=L\operatorname{diag}(q_1,\ldots,q_r)L^{\mathsf T}\succ0,\qquad
 L^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(m_{e1},\ldots,m_{er})\ge0. \tag{19}
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\) holds.  The depth-\(r\) leaves are therefore exactly \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\), and \(\text{thm:sharp-target-fiber}\) identifies this observable family with \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\).

By (13), all reaching orders for a subset share one memoized state.  There are at most \(\binom d k\) subsets of size \(k\), so at most \(\sum_{k=0}^r\binom d k\) states are visited, and the recursion terminates after depth \(r\).  Finally, \(\text{def:complete-classification}\) defines \(\mathcal C(\theta)\) and \(\mathcal P(\theta)\) as respectively the intersection and union of this exact leaf family, proving the last assertion.

We first verify that the feasible set is nonempty; this is required because an approximate minimizer cannot otherwise be selected.  Let
\[
 a=\frac{m+M}{2},\qquad q=\frac{M-m}{4},\qquad
 Z_0=aI_d,\qquad Z_1=Z_0+q\operatorname{diag}(I_r,0),\qquad Z_e=Z_0\ (e\ge2).
\]
Because \(0<m<M\), all eigenvalues lie in \([m,M]\).  The reference difference has rank \(r\), every later difference has range in its range, and the first \(r\) labels with their natural order have certificate \(L=I_r\), \(D=qI_r\), \(\Lambda_1=qI_r\), and \(\Lambda_e=0\) for \(e\ge2\).  Thus this tuple belongs to \(\Theta_K\).

Next we expose the finite-dimensional real-algebraic structure rather than assuming an attained projection.  Positive semidefiniteness and positive definiteness are finite principal-minor inequalities.  Exact rank \(r\) is expressed by vanishing of all \((r+1)\)-minors and strict positivity of the sum of squares of all \(r\)-minors.  Given exact reference rank \(r\), the common-range condition is expressed by vanishing of all \((r+1)\)-minors of the matrices obtained by adjoining columns of \(Z_e-Z_0\) to \(Z_1-Z_0\).  For each of the finitely many choices of \(T\) and \(t\), the certificate is expressed using real witness variables \(L,D,(\Lambda_e)_e\), the polynomial equations
\[
 Q_{tt}=LDL^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 P_t(Z_e-Z_0)P_t^{\mathsf T}=L\Lambda_eL^{\mathsf T}, \tag{20}
\]
together with unit-lower and diagonal zero equations, strict positivity of the diagonal of \(D\), and nonnegativity of the diagonals of \(\Lambda_e\).  Hence membership in \(\Theta_K\), with one ordered witness retained, is a finite Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and inequalities after existentially eliminating the displayed witness variables.

Let
\[
 v(s)=\inf_{\xi\in\Theta_K}\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w^2.
\]
It is finite because \(\Theta_K\ne\varnothing\).  Its graph is characterized without attainment by
\[
 v\ge0,\qquad
 \bigl(\forall\xi\in\Theta_K\bigr)\ v\le\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w^2,\qquad
 \bigl(\forall u>v\bigr)\bigl(\exists\xi\in\Theta_K\bigr)\
       \lVert\xi-s\rVert_w^2<u. \tag{21}
\]
All expressions in (21) are polynomial after expanding the weighted Frobenius norm.  A cylindrical algebraic decomposition eliminates the quantified coordinates in (20)--(21), so the graph of \(v\) and the augmented graph consisting of
\((s,\zeta,T,t,L,D,(\Lambda_e)_e)\) satisfying (20), \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\), and
\[
 \lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w^2<\bigl(\sqrt{v(s)}+\epsilon\bigr)^2 \tag{22}
\]
are semialgebraic; the square root in (22) is encoded by an auxiliary \(\rho\ge0\) with \(\rho^2=v(s)\).  Every fiber of this augmented graph is nonempty.  Indeed, by the defining property of an infimum, for every \(\epsilon>0\) some \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\) has \(\lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w<\sqrt{v(s)}+\epsilon\), and membership supplies one of the finitely many ordered witnesses.

It remains to justify the section asserted by \(\text{def:certified-approximate-selector}\).  In the fixed cylindrical decomposition, order the finitely many cells.  Over each base cell choose the first cell having a nonempty fiber.  A cylindrical cell in one new coordinate is either the graph of one of its semialgebraic boundary functions or a band between two such functions.  Select the boundary value in the graph case, the midpoint for two finite boundaries, the lower boundary plus one or the upper boundary minus one for a one-sided band, and zero for a two-sided unbounded band.  Repeating this coordinate by coordinate produces a semialgebraic point in the chosen fiber.  Induction over the finitely many coordinates gives a semialgebraic section of the augmented graph, including the discrete ordered-certificate branch.  Its covariance component is the map \(s_{\epsilon}\).

By construction,
\[
 s_{\epsilon}(s)\in\Theta_K,\qquad
 \lVert s_{\epsilon}(s)-s\rVert_w
 <\inf_{\xi\in\Theta_K}\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w+\epsilon, \tag{23}
\]
and the retained variables satisfy (20), hence certify the returned tuple.  Finally, a semialgebraic map is Borel measurable: the inverse image of an open coordinate box is the projection of its semialgebraic graph intersected with that box, hence is semialgebraic by the same cylindrical elimination, and coordinate boxes generate the Euclidean Borel sigma-field.  This proves all parts of the lemma without assuming that the infimum in (21) is attained.

For a fixed environment suppress the index \(e\), write
\(\widehat\Sigma=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_iY_i^{\mathsf T}\), and diagonalize
\(\Sigma=O\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_d)O^{\mathsf T}\).  Writing \(Y=O\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\sigma_j})Z\) with independent standard normal coordinates, differentiation of the one-dimensional moment generating function gives
\(\mathbb E Z_j^2=1\), \(\mathbb E Z_j^4=3\), and independence gives
\[
 \mathbb E(Y_jY_kY_lY_m)
 =\Sigma_{jk}\Sigma_{lm}+\Sigma_{jl}\Sigma_{km}+\Sigma_{jm}\Sigma_{kl}. \tag{24}
\]
Consequently, independence across observations and a direct sum over matrix entries yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Sigma}\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\rVert_F^2
 =\frac1n\sum_{j,k}\operatorname{Var}(Y_jY_k)
 =\frac1n\left\{(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma)^2+\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^2)\right\}. \tag{25}
\]
Under \(\Sigma\preceq MI_d\), the right side multiplied by \(n\) is at most
\(M^2(d^2+d)=M^2d(d+1)\).  Summing (25) over the independent environments proves, uniformly over \(\theta\in\Theta_K\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\theta}\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w^2
 \le(E+1)M^2d(d+1)=V_{\max}. \tag{26}
\]
Markov's inequality and \(c_{\alpha}^2=V_{\max}/\alpha\) therefore give
\[
 \Pr_{\theta}\!\left(\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w\le c_{\alpha}\right)
 \ge1-\alpha. \tag{27}
\]

On the event in (27), the true tuple satisfies the covariance box constraints and belongs to \(W_n\), so
\(\theta\in R_n\cap\Theta_K\).  The sharp-fiber theorem gives
\(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\).  Since the latter family is one of the terms in the union defining \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n}\), and \(h(\theta)\) is one of the values defining \(\mathcal H_n\),
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n},
 \qquad h(\theta)\in\mathcal H_n. \tag{28}
\]
Combining (27)--(28) proves the asserted uniform joint coverage.

For every sample, \(\text{lem:measurable-certified-selection}\), with \(\epsilon=1\), gives
\(\widetilde\theta_n=s_1(\widehat\Sigma)\in\Theta_K\).  Since this point is included in \(R_n\), the intersection \(R_n\cap\Theta_K\) is never empty.  The selector is Borel measurable.  Moreover, membership of any fixed target set or fixed value of \(h\) in the reported objects is an existential statement over the semialgebraic certificate and region constraints; cylindrical elimination makes each such event Borel.  Thus the finite-valued reporting rule is measurable.

Finally, suppose the rule reports a singleton classification different from \(h(\theta)\).  On the event in (27), (28) puts \(h(\theta)\) in \(\mathcal H_n\), so a singleton \(\mathcal H_n\) could only equal \(\{h(\theta)\}\).  An incorrect report is therefore contained in the complement of (27), whose probability is at most \(\alpha\).  This proves the finite-sample honesty statement.

Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_K\) and let
\(Z=\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w\).  On \(Z\le x\), every \(\zeta\in W_n\) obeys, by the triangle inequality,
\[
 \lVert\zeta-\theta\rVert_w
 \le\lVert\zeta-\widehat\Sigma\rVert_w
   +\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w
 \le c_{\alpha}+x. \tag{29}
\]
Because \(\theta\in\Theta_K\), the infimum in the selector inequality is at most \(Z\).  The strict approximate-fit property with tolerance one therefore gives
\[
 \lVert\widetilde\theta_n-\widehat\Sigma\rVert_w<Z+1,
 \qquad
 \lVert\widetilde\theta_n-\theta\rVert_w<2Z+1\le2x+1. \tag{30}
\]
Equations (29)--(30) imply the claimed non-strict bound
\[
 \sup_{\zeta\in R_n}\lVert\zeta-\theta\rVert_w
 \le\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}. \tag{31}
\]

For any symmetric tuple \(H=(H_e)_e\) and any \(\theta\in\Theta_K\), put
\(K_e=\Sigma_e^{-1/2}H_e\Sigma_e^{-1/2}\).  Then
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_e^{-1}H_e\Sigma_e^{-1}H_e)=\lVert K_e\rVert_F^2.
\]
Since \(mI_d\preceq\Sigma_e\preceq MI_d\), the identities
\(H_e=\Sigma_e^{1/2}K_e\Sigma_e^{1/2}\) and the operator-norm inequality for the Frobenius norm give
\[
 \frac1M\lVert H_e\rVert_F\le\lVert K_e\rVert_F
 \le\frac1m\lVert H_e\rVert_F.
\]
After weighting and summing,
\[
 \frac{1}{\sqrt2 M}\lVert H\rVert_w
 \le\lVert H\rVert_{I,n,\theta}
 \le\frac{1}{\sqrt2 m}\lVert H\rVert_w. \tag{32}
\]

Suppose the strict separation inequality in the theorem holds.  For every
\(\zeta\in R_n\cap\Theta_K\), (31)--(32) imply
\[
 \lVert\zeta-\theta\rVert_{I,n,\theta}
 \le\frac{\lVert\zeta-\theta\rVert_w}{\sqrt2m}
 <\delta_n(\theta). \tag{33}
\]
By the definition of \(\delta_n(\theta)\), no point satisfying (33) can belong to
\(\mathcal A_h(\theta)\).  Hence every point in \(R_n\cap\Theta_K\) has classification \(h(\theta)\).  This intersection is nonempty by \(\text{thm:honest-family-confidence}\), so
\(\mathcal H_n=\{h(\theta)\}\) and the singleton rule reports correctly.

The moment calculation (24)--(26), applied with threshold \(x\), gives
\[
 \Pr_{\theta}(Z>x)\le \frac{\mathbb EZ^2}{x^2}
 \le\frac{V_{\max}}{x^2}. \tag{34}
\]
This is the asserted failure bound.  Taking \(x=c_{\alpha}\), the radius in (31) is at most
\(2c_{\alpha}+1\), while (34) equals \(\alpha\); this proves the stated finite-sample consequence.

For a sequence with \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\to\infty\), choose deterministic \(x_n\to\infty\) with
\(x_n/\delta_n(\theta_n)\to0\).  Then the strict separation condition holds eventually, whereas (34) tends to zero.  If a subclass satisfies
\(D_n:=\inf_{\theta\text{ in the subclass}}\delta_n(\theta)\to\infty\), the common choice
\(x_n=\sqrt{D_n}\) has the same two properties, proving the asserted uniformity.

Fix \(C<\infty\), and let \(\theta_n\in\Theta_K\) satisfy \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\le C\).  By the definition of the infimum, choose
\(\zeta_n=(Z_{0n},\ldots,Z_{En})\in\Theta_K\) such that
\[
 h(\zeta_n)\ne h(\theta_n),
 \qquad
 \lVert\zeta_n-\theta_n\rVert_{I,n,\theta_n}<C+1. \tag{35}
\]
This choice does not assume that the opposite-classification set is closed or that the infimum is attained.

We next obtain a uniform likelihood-ratio moment bound.  Put \(R=M/m>1\) and choose \(p>1\) so close to one that
\(p-(p-1)R>0\).  For one observation, with covariance \(\Sigma\) under the denominator law and covariance \(Z\) under the numerator law, let
\(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d\) be the eigenvalues of
\(\Sigma^{-1/2}Z\Sigma^{-1/2}\).  The covariance bounds put them in \([R^{-1},R]\).  Whitening the Gaussian density and evaluating the product of one-dimensional Gaussian integrals gives, for
\(L=dN(0,Z)/dN(0,\Sigma)\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Sigma}L^p
 =\prod_{j=1}^d
 \lambda_j^{-(p-1)/2}\{p-(p-1)\lambda_j\}^{-1/2}. \tag{36}
\]
The denominator is positive by the choice of \(p\).  If
\[
 g_p(\lambda)=-\frac{p-1}{2}\log\lambda
 -\frac12\log\{p-(p-1)\lambda\},
\]
then \(g_p(1)=g_p'(1)=0\), and \(g_p''\) is bounded above in absolute value by a finite constant \(K_0=K_0(p,R)\) on \([R^{-1},R]\).  Taylor's theorem therefore gives
\(g_p(\lambda)\le K_0(\lambda-1)^2/2\).

For the independent product samples, multiply (36) over observations and environments.  Since
\[
 \sum_j(\lambda_{ej}-1)^2
 =\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Sigma_{en}^{-1}(Z_{en}-\Sigma_{en})
          \Sigma_{en}^{-1}(Z_{en}-\Sigma_{en})\right],
\]
equation (35) implies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\theta_n}\left(\frac{dP_{\zeta_n}}{dP_{\theta_n}}\right)^p
 \le \exp\!\left(K_0\lVert\zeta_n-\theta_n\rVert_{I,n,\theta_n}^2\right)
 \le K_C:=\exp\{K_0(C+1)^2\}<\infty. \tag{37}
\]
The constant is independent of \(n\), the allocation, and the selected pair of tuples.

Let \(A_n\) be the event that the possibly abstaining rule reports exactly \(h(\theta_n)\).  Because this classification is wrong under \(\zeta_n\), uniform \(\alpha\)-honesty gives
\(P_{\zeta_n}(A_n)\le\alpha\).  With
\(L_n=dP_{\zeta_n}/dP_{\theta_n}\), H\"older's inequality and (37) give
\[
 1-\alpha
 \le P_{\zeta_n}(A_n^{\mathsf c})
 =\mathbb E_{\theta_n}[L_n\mathbf 1_{A_n^{\mathsf c}}]
 \le K_C^{1/p}P_{\theta_n}(A_n^{\mathsf c})^{(p-1)/p}. \tag{38}
\]
Thus
\[
 P_{\theta_n}(A_n)
 \le1-\kappa,\qquad
 \kappa=(1-\alpha)^{p/(p-1)}K_C^{-1/(p-1)}>0. \tag{39}
\]
Here \(p\) and \(K_C\) depend only on \(C,\alpha,m,M,d,E\) (the displayed bound in fact needs no additional dependence on \(d,E\)).  Equation (39) is the claimed uniform obstruction to correct certification at bounded information distance.

The vectors \(a\) and \(b\) are linearly independent, so
\(Q=aa^{\mathsf T}+bb^{\mathsf T}\) is positive semidefinite of rank two.  For \(|\gamma|<1\), both coefficients in
\(\Delta_2(\gamma)=2aa^{\mathsf T}+(2+\gamma)bb^{\mathsf T}\) are positive, and its range is contained in \(\operatorname{span}\{a,b\}=\operatorname{range}(Q)\).  The fixed baseline is positive definite by \(\text{def:four-node-collision-path}\).  Hence the sharp-fiber theorem applies.

All six two-by-two principal determinants of \(Q\), in the order
\(12,13,14,23,24,34\), are
\[
 1,\ 1,\ 4,\ 1,\ 1,\ 9, \tag{40}
\]
and its diagonal entries are positive, so every ordered principal block is positive definite.  If the first pivot is label \(1\), direct \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) elimination gives, for second labels \(2,3,4\), respectively,
\[
 D_t=\operatorname{diag}(1,1),\quad
 D_t=\operatorname{diag}(1,1),\quad
 D_t=\operatorname{diag}(1,4),
\]
and
\[
 \Lambda_{2,t}=\operatorname{diag}(2,2+\gamma),\quad
 \Lambda_{2,t}=\operatorname{diag}(2,2+\gamma),\quad
 \Lambda_{2,t}=\operatorname{diag}(2,8+4\gamma). \tag{41}
\]
These matrices are entrywise positive for \(|\gamma|<1\), so the three pairs containing label \(1\) are certified.

For an order beginning at \(j\in\{2,3,4\}\), the transformed off-diagonal entry of \(\Lambda_{2,t}\), divided by \(\gamma\), is as follows:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 j&\multicolumn{3}{c}{\text{second label and coefficient}}\\ \hline
 2&1:-\tfrac12&3:-\tfrac12&4:\tfrac12\\
 3&1:-\tfrac25&2:\tfrac25&4:\tfrac65\\
 4&1:-\tfrac45&2:-\tfrac25&3:-\tfrac65
\end{array} \tag{42}
\]
Each entry in (42) follows by substituting the displayed \(Q\) and \(\Delta_2(\gamma)\) into the two-dimensional elimination formula
\(L=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\Q_{kj}/Q_{jj}&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) and multiplying \(L^{-1}\Delta_2[\{j,k\},\{j,k\}]L^{-\mathsf T}\).  Every coefficient is nonzero.  Thus, when \(\gamma\ne0\), no ordering beginning in \(2,3,4\) is a certificate, and (41) proves
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta_\gamma)
 =\{\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{1,4\}\}. \tag{43}
\]
When \(\gamma=0\), one has \(\Delta_2=2Q\); for every order, its transformed block is \(2D_t\), so (40) certifies all six pairs.  The sharp-fiber theorem converts these algebraic fibers into the asserted causal fibers.  Taking intersections and unions in (43) and at the collision gives the two displayed values of \(h\).  The same factors give a legal realization with target \(\{1,2\}\), reference increments \((1,1)\), and second-environment increments \((2,2+\gamma)\), so positivity for \(|\gamma|<1\) also verifies the stated legality of the path.

We prove the distance bounds under the added bounded-class premise.  Let
\[
 D(\zeta,\theta)=\left(\sum_{e=0}^2\lVert Z_e-\Sigma_e\rVert_F^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
At \(\theta_0\), all six determinants in (40) are strictly positive.  Choose a fixed neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) of \(\theta_0\) on which they remain positive.  For \(j=2,3,4\), define the polynomial
\[
 f_j(\zeta)=Q_{jj}(Z_2-Z_0)_{1j}-Q_{1j}(Z_2-Z_0)_{jj},
 \quad Q=Z_1-Z_0.
\]
Direct substitution gives
\[
 f_2(\theta_\gamma)=-\gamma,\qquad
 f_3(\theta_\gamma)=-2\gamma,\qquad
 f_4(\theta_\gamma)=-4\gamma. \tag{44}
\]
On the closure of a smaller bounded neighborhood, these polynomials have bounded gradients.  Hence there is \(K<\infty\) such that
\[
 \max_{j=2,3,4}|f_j(\zeta)-f_j(\theta_\gamma)|
 \le K D(\zeta,\theta_\gamma) \tag{45}
\]
for \(\zeta,\theta_\gamma\in\mathcal U\).

Suppose \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\cap\mathcal U\) and
\(D(\zeta,\theta_\gamma)<|\gamma|/(2K)\).  Equations (44)--(45) make every \(f_j(\zeta)\), \(j=2,3,4\), nonzero.  The first-pivot proportionality equation for a pivot \(j\) would imply \(f_j(\zeta)=0\) by taking its row \(1\); thus no certificate begins at \(2,3,4\).  Since \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\), at least one certificate exists, and it must begin at \(1\).  After this pivot, the reference residual has rank one.  Every remaining reference diagonal is positive because the six principal determinants remain positive in \(\mathcal U\).  Also, existence of a certificate and range reconstruction express every full shift as a nonnegative sum of the same factor columns, so its residual is positive semidefinite and its range lies in the rank-one reference residual range.  It must therefore equal a nonnegative scalar multiple of that reference residual.  Every remaining label is consequently an admissible second pivot.  The fiber is exactly the star in (43), and \(h(\zeta)=h(\theta_\gamma)\).

Shrinking the neighborhood once more, points outside it have a fixed positive \(D\)-distance from \(\theta_\gamma\) for all sufficiently small \(|\gamma|\).  Combining this fact with the preceding paragraph gives a constant \(c_0>0\) such that every \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\) with different classification satisfies
\[
 D(\zeta,\theta_\gamma)\ge c_0|\gamma|. \tag{46}
\]
For equal sample sizes, the covariance bounds imply directly, by writing
\(H_e=\Sigma_e^{1/2}(\Sigma_e^{-1/2}H_e\Sigma_e^{-1/2})\Sigma_e^{1/2}\), that
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n}{\sqrt2M}D(\zeta,\theta_\gamma)
 \le \lVert\zeta-\theta_\gamma\rVert_{I,n,\theta_\gamma}
 \le \frac{\sqrt n}{\sqrt2m}D(\zeta,\theta_\gamma). \tag{47}
\]
The left inequality in (47) and (46) imply
\[
 \delta_n(\theta_\gamma)\ge \frac{c_0}{\sqrt2M}\sqrt n\,|\gamma|. \tag{48}
\]
For the reverse bound, the bounded-class premise puts \(\theta_0\in\Theta_K\), and its classification differs from that at every nonzero \(\gamma\).  Only environment \(2\) changes between these tuples, by \(\gamma bb^{\mathsf T}\).  The right inequality in (47) therefore gives
\[
 \delta_n(\theta_\gamma)
 \le\lVert\theta_0-\theta_\gamma\rVert_{I,n,\theta_\gamma}
 \le\frac{\sqrt n}{\sqrt2m}|\gamma|\lVert bb^{\mathsf T}\rVert_F. \tag{49}
\]
Equations (48)--(49) establish the claimed constants \(0<c<C<\infty\).

Assume \(r=1\) and \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\ne\varnothing\).  The sharp-fiber theorem gives a certified singleton \(\{k\}\).  Its realization, or equivalently range reconstruction applied to its certificate, shows that
\(Q=aa^{\mathsf T}d\) for some \(d>0\); hence \(Q\) is positive semidefinite of rank one.  For every \(e\), symmetry and
\(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)=\operatorname{span}\{a\}\) imply
\(\Delta_e=c_eQ\) for a scalar \(c_e\).  At the certified coordinate \(k\), the scalar certificate equals
\(\Delta_{e,kk}/Q_{kk}=c_e\), so nonnegativity of that certificate gives \(c_e\ge0\).

Now fix any label \(j\).  For the one-element order \(t=(j)\), the reference block is the scalar \(Q_{jj}\).  It is positive exactly when \(Q_{jj}>0\); in that case its unit-lower factor is \(L_t=(1)\), and every transformed block is the scalar
\[
 \Lambda_{e,t}=\Delta_{e,jj}=c_eQ_{jj}\ge0.
\]
Thus \(\{j\}\) is certified exactly when \(Q_{jj}>0\).  Applying the sharp-fiber equality proves
\(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{\{j\}:Q_{jj}>0\}\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every \(x>0\), on the event \(\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w\le x\), every point of \(R_n\) is within weighted distance at most \(\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}\) of \(\theta\).  Hence, if \(\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}<\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)\), the singleton rule based on \(\mathcal H_n\) reports \(h(\theta)\), and its failure probability is at most \(V_{\max}/x^2\).  In particular, \(\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)>2c_{\alpha}+1\) implies correct reporting with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).  For every sequence \(\theta_n\in\Theta_K\) with \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\to\infty\), the rule reports \(h(\theta_n)\) with probability tending to one, uniformly over subclasses on which the infimum of \(\delta_n\) diverges.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The raw covariance region is a closed ball, so its triangle bound is non-strict.  Replacing only the first strict inequality by a non-strict one is necessary and leaves every subsequent strict separation, probability bound, and consistency conclusion unchanged.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Along the legal path \(\theta_{\gamma}\), \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta_{\gamma})=\{\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{1,4\}\}\) and \(h(\theta_{\gamma})=(\{1\},\{1,2,3,4\})\) for \(\gamma\ne0\), whereas at \(\gamma=0\) all six two-element target sets are compatible and \(h(\theta_0)=(\varnothing,\{1,2,3,4\})\).  If the fixed constants \(m,M\) admit \(\gamma_0>0\) such that \(\theta_{\gamma}\in\Theta_K\) for every \(|\gamma|\le\gamma_0\), then, for equal environment sample sizes, there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c\sqrt n|\gamma|\le\delta_n(\theta_{\gamma})\le C\sqrt n|\gamma|\) for all sufficiently small nonzero \(\gamma\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The information distance is defined relative to the fixed bounded covariance class.  The unqualified path claim is false for an arbitrarily narrow covariance box, because the fixed nonzero reference shift cannot fit inside it.  The added local-membership premise is exactly what permits the collision tuple to witness the upper bound and the covariance eigenvalue bounds to control the lower bound; it narrows the rate clause without changing the exact fiber calculation.

proposed.statement: Along the legal path \(\theta_{\gamma}\), \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta_{\gamma})=\{\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{1,4\}\}\) and \(h(\theta_{\gamma})=(\{1\},\{1,2,3,4\})\) for \(\gamma\ne0\), whereas at \(\gamma=0\) all six two-element target sets are compatible and \(h(\theta_0)=(\varnothing,\{1,2,3,4\})\).  If the fixed constants \(m,M\) admit \(\gamma_0>0\) such that \(\theta_{\gamma}\in\Theta_K\) for every \(|\gamma|\le\gamma_0\), then, for equal environment sample sizes, there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c\sqrt n|\gamma|\le\delta_n(\theta_{\gamma})\le C\sqrt n|\gamma|\) for all sufficiently small nonzero \(\gamma\).
proposed.justification: The witness proves that profile collision changes compulsory labels and that the abstract information distance has a concrete first-order scale.
proposed.gap: Bacchiocchi et al. study rotation sets at repeated HSVAR eigenvalues, but not a legal acyclic SCM path whose complete labeled target family changes with a computed Gaussian-information rate.
proposed.consumer: The example is an early kill test for implementations of augmentation, classification, and pivot memoization in the smallest nontrivial case.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed rate statement directly names the covariance bounds and bounded class, and its proof uses the bounded-class and information-distance definitions; this replacement makes the dependency and free-symbol metadata match the corrected claim.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine a sequence-specific Gaussian tangent-cone minimax value and an attaining measurable classifier after specifying every incident classification cone; alternatively prove a universality theorem showing that those values depend only on the finite local information limit.
open_obligations.obstruction: The scalar information distance retains only nearest-opposite-classification distance.  It discards the number, angles, and multiplicities of incident semialgebraic tangent cones, while Gaussian minimax testing values generally depend on that geometry.  The frozen core supplies no hypothesis equating the tangent experiments of all regular sequences, so a universal one-variable envelope cannot be derived from the declared primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced each fixed regular sequence formally to testing a finite union of tangent cones in its Gaussian covariance shift experiment and compared the data retained by that experiment with the scalar distance.  The reduction exposes additional cone geometry not encoded by that distance, preventing a common optimization or a uniform attaining rule from being specified.
open_obligations.partial_result: For any fixed regular sequence for which the local experiments and all incident semialgebraic tangent cones are specified, the handle reduces correct certification to a Gaussian-shift testing problem with null and alternative regions given by those cones.  The scalar limit \(c=\lim\delta_n(\theta_n)\) records only the nearest alternative distance; it does not record the number, angles, or multiplicities of incident cones.  Those geometric data enter the minimax testing value, so the frozen core does not determine one universal function \(\beta^{\star}(c)\) or an attaining classifier uniformly over every regular sequence.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\lambda^{\pm}\) and \(\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}\) for the two increment arrays in \(\text{def:restriction-boundary-witnesses}\), and put \(\lambda^{w}_0=0\) for \(w\in\{\pm,\mathrm{split}\}\).  We first construct the primitive noises, so that validity of the displayed covariance tuples is not being inferred merely from their definitions.  For each \(w\), let all coordinates of \(h_e,z_e,v_e\), over \(e\in\{0,1,2\}\), be independent standard normal random variables, and define
\[
 H_e=h_e,\qquad
 \varepsilon_e=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\sqrt{\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^w_e}\right)z_e,
 \qquad
 \eta_e=2^{-1/2}v_e.
\]
Here the square root is taken coordinatewise.  It is well defined for the signed witness because
\[
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\pm}_0=(3/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\pm}_1=(5/2,5/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\pm}_2=(1,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},
\]
and it is well defined for the split-reference witness because
\[
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_0=(3/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_1=(5/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_2=(3/2,5/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus every structural-noise covariance used in either witness is positive definite.  Set \(\Omega_{H,\mu}=I_3\).  The construction gives centered jointly Gaussian primitive vectors, mutual independence of \(H_e\), the coordinates of \(\varepsilon_e\), and \(\eta_e\), the stationary latent covariance \(I_3\), and the stationary diagonal measurement covariance \(I_3/2\succ0\).  Moreover, \(B_{\mu}=0\) is acyclic, \(U_{\mu}=(I_3-B_{\mu})^{-1}=I_3\), \(C_{\mu}=0\), and every coordinate of \(\omega_{0,\mu}\) equals \(3/2>0\).  Hence, by independence and the definition of \(Y_e\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)
 =U_{\mu}\!\left(C_{\mu}\Omega_{H,\mu}C_{\mu}^{\mathsf T}
   +\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^w_e)\right)U_{\mu}^{\mathsf T}
   +\Omega_{\eta,\mu}
 =\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^w_e)+\tfrac12 I_3.
\]
This yields exactly the three covariance matrices specified for each tuple in \(\text{def:restriction-boundary-witnesses}\).

For \(\theta^{\pm}\), the declared target set is \(T_{\mu}=\{1,2\}\), so \(|T_{\mu}|=2=r\); every increment at coordinate \(3\) is zero; and \(\lambda^{\pm}_{11}=\lambda^{\pm}_{12}=1>0\).  Thus target cardinality, exclusion of off-target shifts, and the common-reference condition all hold.  The sole failed member condition of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\) is nonnegativity, because \(\lambda^{\pm}_{21}=-1/2<0\).  In particular, this failure does not invalidate a primitive covariance: the preceding display gives its first variance as \(3/2-1/2=1>0\).

The observable shifts of this witness are
\[
 Q=\Delta_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,0),
 \qquad
 \Delta_2=\operatorname{diag}(-1/2,0,0).
\]
For the order \(t=(1,2)\), one has \(Q_{tt}=I_2\).  To make the \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) step explicit, write
\[
 L_t=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\ \ell&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad D_t=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_2),\qquad d_1,d_2>0.
\]
The equality \(L_tD_tL_t^{\mathsf T}=I_2\) gives successively \(d_1=1\), \(d_1\ell=0\), and \(d_1\ell^2+d_2=1\), hence \(L_t=I_2\) and \(D_t=I_2\).  Therefore
\[
 \Lambda_{2,t}
 =L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_2P_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(-1/2,0).
\]
It is diagonal but is not entrywise nonnegative.  The only other ordering is \(t'=(2,1)\).  Again \(Q_{t't'}=I_2\), the same calculation gives \(L_{t'}=D_{t'}=I_2\), and
\[
 \Lambda_{2,t'}=\operatorname{diag}(0,-1/2),
\]
which is also not entrywise nonnegative.  Consequently no ordering of the true target set satisfies \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta^{\pm},\{1,2\},t)\).  This proves, without identifying the causal target with the observable predicate, that after signed shifts are admitted the nonnegative-diagonal condition is not necessary for compatibility with the true causal target.

For \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\), the same construction verifies acyclicity, centered Gaussianity, independence, stationarity, and strict positivity of both structural and measurement noises.  Again \(T_{\mu}=\{1,2\}\) has cardinality \(r=2\), all coordinate-\(3\) increments vanish, and every target increment is nonnegative.  Coordinate \(1\) changes in environment \(1\), while coordinate \(2\) changes in environment \(2\), so the declared target set is exactly the set of changing coordinates.  The common-reference condition alone fails, since \(\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_{12}=0\).

Here
\[
 Q=\Delta_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,0,0),
 \qquad
 \Delta_2=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,0).
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=1<r\).  Every size-two principal block of \(Q\) is either the zero matrix or, up to simultaneous row and column permutation, \(\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\).  Each such block has a nonzero null vector and therefore is not positive definite.  Hence no size-two candidate, including the true target \(\{1,2\}\), can pass the positive-definite reference-block requirement in \(\operatorname{Cert}\).

The failed range reconstruction is also explicit:
\[
 \operatorname{range}(Q)=\operatorname{span}\{(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{range}(\Delta_2)=\operatorname{span}\{(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\},
\]
so \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_2)\nsubseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\).  No procedure using only the reference range can recover the second changing direction in this witness.  By contrast, the multi-environment aggregate
\[
 \Delta_1+\Delta_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,0)
\]
has rank \(2=r\) and carries both directions.  Thus an extension covering this design must replace the single-reference carrier by an object incorporating more than one environment.  Likewise, in the signed case strict validity of the primitive structural covariance requires, for each target coordinate \(j\), the inequalities
\[
 \omega_{0,\mu,j}>0,
 \qquad
 \omega_{0,\mu,j}+\lambda_{ej}>0
 \quad\text{for every }e,
\]
rather than \(\lambda_{ej}\ge0\).  These are precisely the baseline-variance feasibility inequalities exhibited by \(\theta^{\pm}\).  The two witnesses therefore establish all claimed boundary failures and the stated forms of the necessary replacements.
